test-bloat-00.title: Byte-identical sixteen-field HydroPenalties fixture literal duplicated between the resolved-penalties and system test modules while the crate's test-support surface already owns the penalty constructors

The only shared constructor at the pin is HydroPenalties::uniform at entities/hydro.rs:97-121, gated on test-or-test-support, and it emits one value for all sixteen fields; with eleven distinct values the update-syntax rest pattern the crate already uses at test_support.rs:217 and entities/hydro.rs:325 would still spell thirteen overrides, so no existing constructor expresses this sequence. test-bloat-01.title: Debug-non-empty assertions in the training-event test module can only fail if the derive itself is broken, so they cannot fail on the variant data they name
test-bloat-01.survivingClaim: Narrowing the registered TD-001 roster by one member: at the pin exactly two bodies in crates/cobre-core/src/constraints/training_event.rs are fully derive-discharged, all_variants_clone (:633-639) and all_variants_debug_non_empty (:641-647), because each asserts only that a derived Debug rendering is non-empty and both types derive Debug with no manual impl (:163-164, :91-92). stopping_rule_result_debug_non_empty (:723-732) belongs OUTSIDE that set: beyond the derive-discharged :730 it asserts at :731 that the rendering contains the rule_name value, which no derive guarantees for arbitrary field values. Second, narrower correction to the candidate's counter-evidence: of the two tests it cites as load-bearing only forward_pass_complete_fields_accessible (:649) destructures without a rest pattern, while stage_row_selection_record_fields_accessible (:914-940) gets its compile-time tripwire from a ten-field struct literal plus field echoes, not from a destructure.
test-bloat-01.coverageNeutralShape: consolidation of the two derive-discharged bodies into one value-sensitive body over the same fixture: all_variants_clone (:633-639) and all_variants_debug_non_empty (:641-647) loop the identical make_all_variants() fixture and terminate in the identical non-emptiness assertion, so they fold into a single loop that clones each variant and asserts the clone's Debug rendering equals the source's, which is the strongest comparison available given the enum derives no PartialEq (:163-164). Every variant of the fixture stays covered, the Clone step is kept and becomes load-bearing for the first time, the non-emptiness assertion is retained alongside so nothing previously asserted is dropped, and stopping_rule_result_debug_non_empty (:723-732) plus all_variants_construct (:623-631) are left untouched. A count-neutral variant of the same shape exists and is equally coverage-neutral: keep both test functions and strengthen each in place against the same clone-versus-source rendering comparison, which leaves the nextest count unchanged and makes the owner question below moot.
test-bloat-01.argument: The core defect is real but the candidate over-reaches on its own roster, and the over-reach is the delta worth recording. Both types carry plain derives at the pin (TrainingEvent at training_event.rs:163-164 derives Clone and Debug only, StoppingRuleResult at :91-92 the same, with no hand-written Debug anywhere in the file), so a derived Debug always emits at least the variant or struct name and a non-emptiness assertion over it is discharged unconditionally by codegen. That reading holds for exactly two bodies: all_variants_clone at :633-639, whose sole assertion is that the clone's Debug rendering is non-empty, and all_variants_debug_non_empty at :641-647, whose sole assertion is the same over the source. It does NOT hold for the third body the title and the seed roster sweep in. stopping_rule_result_debug_non_empty carries two assertions, not one: :730 is the derive-discharged non-emptiness check, but :731 asserts that the rendering contains the rule_name value, which is value-sensitive and fails if the field value changes or a manual Debug omits it, so that test is outside the derive-discharged set at the pin. The candidate's own counter-evidence is also mis-mechanised on one anchor: forward_pass_complete_fields_accessible at :649-673 does destructure with no rest pattern, but stage_row_selection_record_fields_accessible at :914-940 never destructures, it builds a struct literal naming all ten fields and then echoes each through field access, so its compile-time tripwire comes from struct-literal exhaustiveness rather than from a rest-pattern-free pattern. The conclusion that both are load-bearing survives; the stated mechanism for one of them does not. all_variants_construct at :623-631 pins the fixture at sixteen variants and stays out of the claim, as the seed already records. The fix-shape stays inside the crate's own cfg(test) module and proposes no deletion, so the cost-discipline rule at testing.md:113-117 is satisfied rather than strained.

test-bloat-06.definitionScreen: stable (unpaired key: the figure has one definition)
test-bloat-06.argument: Measured over the whole directory at the pin, crates/cobre-io/src/scenarios/ is not a coin-flip. Fourteen files there keep inline test modules whose bodies run from 64 lines (scenarios/mod.rs, mod tests at 236 of 299) up to 561 lines (scenarios/correlation.rs, mod tests at 411 of 971), and the directory's one extracted sibling, scenarios/estimation/tests.rs, is 2978 lines. The split is strictly size-ordered with a 5.3x gap and no file in between, so any threshold placed between the directory's largest inline module and its one sibling reproduces the current layout exactly. A directory whose files straddle a size threshold MUST hold both forms: that is the output of the section 5.1 rule 'inline when the test module is below a fixed threshold, extracted to a sibling tests.rs above it' (docs/design/testing-architecture.md:253-256), not a violation of it. The yardstick's own coin-flip criterion at section 3.2 item 4 (docs/design/testing-architecture.md:146-149) fires on ANTI-monotone splits, and the tree bears that out where the doc points it: in crates/cobre-sddp/src/lp/builder/ the two files with by far the largest inline test volume stayed inline (entries.rs, first inline cfg(test) module at 1680 of 10093 lines; columns.rs, at 1305 of 9319) while the SMALLER template/tests.rs (5356 lines) and layout/tests.rs (3565 lines) were extracted. Applied to scenarios/, that same criterion does not fire, because there the bigger module is the extracted one. Once the size ordering is granted, the only residue is WHERE the boundary sits, and that boundary is the unratified proposal at :253-256 (claimClassRows ta-5.1-homing-threshold, class target, driftIsFinding false, TD-031) whose two legs disagree about both files: under the ~500 test-LOC leg both would extract (561 and 2978 each exceed 500), under the ~40 test-fns leg both would stay inline (correlation.rs carries 16 test functions, the sibling 38). So the sharpening's load-bearing premise, that the residue is threshold-INDEPENDENT, does not hold at the pin. The candidate's supporting figure is also mis-defined: estimation/tests.rs carries 38 test-attribute functions and 64 fn declarations, the extra 26 being helpers, so its '64 test fns' reads a fn-declaration count as a test count, and neither 64 nor the seed's 36 is the test-function figure (38). The crate-scope observation the candidate adds (one sibling against 100 inline cfg(test) files, with twelve inline modules of 1546 to 2586 lines elsewhere in cobre-io) is a real non-uniformity, but it is BROADER than the title rather than narrower, and it is exactly the threshold question section 5.1 leaves open, so it cannot carry a confirmation here.

architecture-01.survivingClaim: Narrowed to the trailing clause of the §2.2 map: the words 'constructing fixtures per-file' at docs/design/testing-architecture.md:78 are contradicted for exactly two crates at the pin, crates/cobre-stochastic/tests/common/mod.rs (261 lines, declared by 8 of the crate's 9 depth-1 binaries) and crates/cobre-io/tests/helpers/mod.rs (204 lines, declared by 6 of 12), and the drift is internal to §2.2 because :72-73 already concedes 'the only LARGE tests/common/ harness'. architecture-02.title: One shared-harness role carries two directory names and three compositions, and the differently-named cobre-io harness is invisible to a migration that greps for tests/common
architecture-02.definitionScreen: stable (definition is a label; the asserted fact does not depend on the denominator)
architecture-02.survivingClaim: Exactly one crate names the shared integration prelude off-convention: crates/cobre-io/tests/helpers/mod.rs, declared 'mod helpers;' by 6 of cobre-io's 12 depth-1 binaries, fills the same source-included prelude role that 33 cobre-sddp and 8 cobre-stochastic binaries reach as tests/common/, and tests/common/ is the only name the pinned cost-discipline bullet (.claude/rules/testing.md:120, :123) and every §2.2 / §5.2 sentence use, so nothing in the tree or the rules leads a reader to cobre-io's prelude without knowing the exception. Struck from the title: the three-composition spread (two of the three are the delivered 2026-09-15 shared-fixture convention at docs/design/reserved-seams-and-deferred-debt.md:1173-1183, the third is the open §5.2 bullet already recorded at docs/design/testing-architecture.md:425-431) and the migration-invisibility harm (the collapse bullet at :417-421 names one directory by crate path, so there is no grep-driven migration).
architecture-02.coverageNeutralShape: re-homing: move cobre-io's shared prelude from crates/cobre-io/tests/helpers/mod.rs to crates/cobre-io/tests/common/mod.rs and change the six 'mod helpers;' declarations (integration.rs:10, invariance.rs:14, load_case_productivity_resolution.rs:9, load_case_scalar_parameters.rs:5, post_study_stages.rs:17, resolver_builder_index_alignment.rs:18) to 'mod common;', so the one directory name the cost-discipline bullet already uses reaches every crate's prelude and one convention statement covers all three. A prelude directory is not a depth-1 tests/*.rs and compiles no binary under either name, so the binary count, the feature-combo count and every assertion are untouched and cargo nextest list reports the same count before and after; no test function is renamed and no fixture body moves.
architecture-02.argument: The naming half holds at the pin and nothing in the tree justifies it; the other two halves are over-reach and are struck. git ls-tree at 077dbe2c shows exactly three shared integration preludes across the workspace: crates/cobre-sddp/tests/common/ (five files, 320 + 383 + 417 + 204 + 181 lines, submodules declared at mod.rs:25-28, StubComm at mod.rs:32), crates/cobre-stochastic/tests/common/mod.rs (261 lines) and crates/cobre-io/tests/helpers/mod.rs (204 lines); 47 depth-1 binaries reach them (33 sddp, 8 stochastic, 6 io). The io module's doc at :1 states only its role ('Fixture builders that construct case directories in a TempDir'); no module doc, no test doc comment, no .claude/rules/testing.md bullet and no docs/design/ sentence states the name choice, and there is no collision forcing it (no 'common' module exists anywhere under crates/cobre-io). The role is identical in all three: each is source-included per binary rather than linked once, which is exactly why each carries a module-level allow(dead_code, unused_imports) with a rationale comment (sddp mod.rs:6, stochastic mod.rs:6, io mod.rs:2-5), and the io and stochastic modules are the same kind of object, a re-export shim over the crate's src test_support plus two or three local case builders. tests/common/ is also the only name the pinned cost-discipline bullet uses (.claude/rules/testing.md:120 and :123) and the only name every §2.2 / §5.2 sentence uses (docs/design/testing-architecture.md:73, :123, :143, :360-362, :419, :428, :580). With no deliberate-and-documented basis, no contract requiring the exception and no sanctioned seam covering it, the naming residue is confirmed as a tree-fact under the §3.2.2 current-state row ('There is no crate testing standard'). What I strike: (1) the composition spread is the recorded outcome of a delivered, ratified fix, not a new smell. docs/design/reserved-seams-and-deferred-debt.md:1173 heads the 2026-09-15 'shared test-fixture surface per type owner' entry as fixed, :1181-1183 records cobre-io's writers and minimal-case corpus hoisted to its src test_support and the cobre-stochastic binaries sharing one tests/common prelude, and :1201-1204 plus docs/design/testing-architecture.md:425-431 record the one remaining open bullet, that cobre-sddp's tests/common/ still holds its own fixture directory. Two of the three compositions are therefore the adopted convention and the third is an already-recorded open bullet. (2) The migration-invisibility harm does not exist at the pin: the §5.2 collapse bullet at :417-421 names a single directory by explicit crate path, the mirror's open-half paragraph repeats that same single scope, and whether the list grows to the other two preludes is an owner call (adjudicate row ta-5.2-adoption-uniform), so no grep-driven repo-wide migration exists to be blind to any directory.

anchors.note: the sibling builder that does have callers, e.g. crates/cobre-sddp/tests/basis_trajectory_probe.rs

over-engineering-00.survivingClaim: Narrowed from the fixture surface to one 23-line item and one condition: `crates/cobre-sddp/src/test_support.rs:177-199` is unreached at the pin AND its only differentiator from `eq` at `:152-171`, the identity default `anticipated_thermal_indices: (0..n_anticipated).collect()`, is a shape no anticipated caller wants — five of the thirteen live anticipated `GeometryDims` literals set `vec![1]` at `n_anticipated: 1` (extraction/tests.rs `:1133`, `:1477`, `:1738`, `:2349`; generic_constraints/tests.rs `:2093`) where identity yields the wrong `vec![0]`, and two need a caller-supplied list (setup/tests.rs `:3490`, `:7646`). The claim does NOT reach `GeometryDims` or its anticipated fields (thirteen live literals), the rest of `test_support.rs`, or `eq`, which has a caller at `crates/cobre-sddp/tests/basis_trajectory_probe.rs:282`.
over-engineering-00.coverageNeutralShape: consolidation — retire the zero-caller `eq_with_anticipated` and leave one `GeometryDims` construction path: `eq` at `:152-171` for the no-anticipated shape, plus the exhaustive or struct-update literal the thirteen anticipated fixtures already use, which is the only form that can express a non-identity `anticipated_thermal_indices`. Not the attacker's second direction (routing the anticipated suite through the constructor), which the five `vec![1]` sites cannot take. No test function, assertion, fixture deck, test binary or `cargo nextest list --features test-support` entry changes; every anticipated fixture keeps the exact dims it asserts on today.

performance-00.argument: The job census holds at the pin: cargo test --workspace at .github/workflows/ci.yml:114, the CLP build and nextest run at :223 and :233, and llvm-cov at :497, none of the three gated by a job-level if condition.
